data.name: Panama
data.summary: Panama has a territorial tax system: foreign dividends, interest and gains on foreign securities are not taxed, and there is no inheritance, gift or wealth tax. Panamanian-source investment income is taxed lightly (10% on local securities gains, 10%/5% final WHT on local dividends). US/EU withholding taxes on the portfolio are a final cost. The balboa (PAB) is at par with the US dollar, which circulates as legal tender.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence (territorial)
regimes.description: Residents and non-residents are taxed only on Panamanian-source income. Foreign dividends, interest and gains on foreign securities are not taxed. Panamanian securities gains 10%; local dividends 10%/5% WHT.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if 183+ days in the current or preceding year, or permanent residence established. Foreign nationals need a residence visa.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on foreign securities are foreign-source and not taxed. Gains on shares, bonds and other securities issued by Panamanian entities: 10% (buyer withholds 5% of price, which the seller may treat as final). Panamanian real estate: 10% of the gain, or the 3% advance on price as final tax.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends are not taxed. Dividends from Panamanian operating companies bear 10% WHT (5% when paid out of foreign-source or exempt income), which is final.

dividends.rate_basis: Deloitte 2026: dividend WHT 10%/5%; 'subsequent distribution not taxed'. Territorial: foreign dividends exempt.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 10% (Panamanian-source profits) / 5% (foreign-source or exempt profits); 20% for bearer shares; higher retaliatory rates (20%/40%) for discriminating jurisdictions.
dividends.treaty_network: 18 treaties; BEPS MLI in force 1 Mar 2021. No US treaty. As a territorial system, Panama gives no unilateral credit, and US/EU withholding on the family's portfolio is final.

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax on worldwide income and assets; the app adds the federal layer. Local tax can generally be credited against US tax on the same foreign-source income only where the US foreign tax credit rules allow. Panama levies no tax on the foreign portfolio, so a US family pays full US rates.

income.name: Panama

income_tax.summary: Territorial tax on Panamanian-source income: 0% up to USD 11,000, 15% to USD 50,000 and 25% above. Employees pay 9.75% social security plus 1.25% educational insurance with no ceiling.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Deloitte states that contributions of independent contractors and professionals 'may vary from 9% to 13.5%' of fees; the top of that range is shown and the tier for a given income was not verified. Whether educational insurance is added for the self-employed is not stated. Professionals (including independents contracted in Panama) face 15% withholding at source on gross fees (Deloitte).
income_tax.local_tax_note: Territorial: residents and non-residents are taxed only on Panamanian-source income (Deloitte; PwC). Employee rate is CSS 9.75% (from April 2025) plus 1.25% educational insurance (PwC). Deductions include mortgage interest up to USD 15,000, medical insurance and expenses, and USD 800 (married filing jointly); not applied to the brackets. No local income surtax.

regimes.name: Short Stay Visa as a Remote Worker (Executive Decree 198 of 2021)
regimes.description: Nine-month stay, extendable once for nine months, for remote workers with a foreign employer or autonomous remote work for clients abroad, earning at least USD 36,000 a year from foreign sources. Holders swear not to work in Panama. The visa itself carries no tax clause: any relief comes from Panama's territorial system (only Panamanian-source income is taxed, Deloitte and PwC 2026), which does not reach pay for work physically performed in Panama, so covers_local_work is false and the regime is not scored as a tax relief.
regimes.duration_note: 9 months plus one 9-month extension. Health insurance for the whole stay is required. A stay beyond 183 days in a calendar year or two makes the person tax resident, which does not change the territorial basis.

sources.title: Kraemer Law: Visa for Remote Workers (Executive Decree 198 of May 7 2021)

open_questions: Kraemer Law does not discuss tax; the 'exempt' treatment follows from Panama's territorial system as described by Deloitte and PwC, not from a visa clause. Neither source defines when remote work done in Panama for a foreign employer is Panamanian-source, so covers_local_work false rests on the general source rule and on there being no statutory exemption; a DGI ruling could change this.
Government fees and the need for a lawyer to file were not verified.
Panama's SEM (multinational headquarters) employee regime is not researched.

succession.name: Panama
succession.summary: There is no fixed share for children, but relatives have a right to maintenance that comes before the will's beneficiaries: children up to age 25, disabled children, parents and the spouse. Panama is the clearest trust-and-foundation jurisdiction here: it has a trust law (Law 1 of 1984), a private interest foundation law (Law 25 of 1995), and the Hague Trusts Convention is in force.
succession.family_claims: Panamanian law gives certain relatives a right to maintenance (children up to 25, disabled children, parents, spouse) that takes precedence over beneficiaries named in a will (secondary source, no article cited).
succession.foreign_law_note: Not sourced: Panama's private international law code (Law 61 of 2015) rule on the law applicable to succession was not read.
succession.trust_note: Hague Trusts Convention: accession 30 Aug 2017, in force 1 Dec 2018 (HCCH table). Trust Law 1 of 1984, as amended by Law 21 of 2017, governs trusts; professional trustees need a licence from the Superintendency of Banks. Private Interest Foundations: Law 25 of 12 June 1995; art. 14 says heirship rules of the founder's or beneficiaries' domicile cannot be enforced against the foundation, but a foreign court applying its own law can still look through it.
open_questions: Civil Code articles on maintenance and any compulsory share were not read; the no-heirship finding rests on two secondary sources.
Law 61 of 2015 (private international law) was not read; foreign_law_choice is unclear.
Whether Panamanian courts would apply art. 14 of Law 25 against a Panamanian-domiciled founder's heirs was not sourced.

immigration.name: Panama
immigration.summary: Panama offers permanent residence by investment (Qualified Investor: USD 300,000 for a new first-sale property, USD 500,000 for resale or securities, from 16 September 2026) and a Friendly Nations visa (USD 200,000, about 50 listed nationalities incl. the US and most EU states, 2 years provisional first). Retirees need a USD 1,000 monthly pension; remote workers USD 36,000 a year. US, EU and other passports are treated alike except for the Friendly Nations list.
immigration.naturalisation: Five years of permanent residence (three for spouses of Panamanians), Spanish test and civics exam, solvency and clean record. Shorter periods for some nationalities by reciprocity.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Sources disagree: one says dual citizenship only with reciprocity countries, another that it is restricted on paper but rarely enforced. Check with a Panamanian lawyer.

routes.name: Qualified Investor visa (permanent residence)
routes.summary: Permanent residence for a property, securities or bank-deposit investment. From 16 September 2026 resale property needs USD 500,000; only a new first-sale property still qualifies at USD 300,000.
routes.requirements: Executive Decree 17 of 8 September 2026 (rules apply from 16 September 2026; earlier filings and binding contracts signed before then may use old thresholds if filed within 6 months). Options: new first-sale real estate USD 300,000; resale real estate USD 500,000; promise-of-sale USD 300,000 backed by an irrevocable bank instrument (max 3 cumulative years); securities USD 500,000 held 5 years; fixed deposit USD 750,000 in a private bank or USD 500,000 in Banco Nacional or Caja de Ahorros, held 5 years. Funds must be the applicant's own foreign-source funds, not a gift from an unrelated party. Annual evidence to MICI. A second source dates the rise to 15 October 2026 and describes the decree differently; treat the exact date as unconfirmed.
routes.investment_options: First-sale real estate USD 300,000; resale real estate USD 500,000; securities USD 500,000; fixed deposit USD 750,000 (private bank) or USD 500,000 (state banks).
routes.physical_presence: One visit every two years is cited by secondary sources; not confirmed
routes.tax_note: Panama taxes only Panama-source income (territorial); permanent residence alone does not decide tax residence (183 days test).

routes.name: Friendly Nations visa
routes.summary: Residence for nationals of about 50 'friendly' countries (including the US and most EU states) who buy USD 200,000 of property, lock a USD 200,000 deposit for 3 years, or hold a formal local job. Starts with 2 years of provisional residence.
routes.requirements: Nationals of about 50 countries (US, Canada, UK, Australia, Japan and 'most of the EU'; the list was not read). One economic tie: real estate of USD 200,000, a fixed deposit of USD 200,000 for 3 years in a general-licence bank, or formal employment with a Panamanian company with a MITRADEL work permit. After 2 years provisional, apply for permanent residence. The sources describe the 2026 changes only vaguely; a possible stricter economic-link test was reported but not confirmed. Not open to nationals outside the friendly list.
routes.physical_presence: Not stated in the sources reviewed
routes.processing_time: Provisional approval 3 to 6 months, permanent step 2 to 4 months (secondary source)
routes.tax_note: Territorial taxation: only Panama-source income is taxed.

sources.title: Panama's Friendly Nations Visa: the 2026 guide

routes.name: Pensionado (retiree) visa
routes.summary: Permanent residence for retirees with a lifetime pension of at least USD 1,000 a month.
routes.requirements: Lifetime pension of at least USD 1,000 a month (USD 12,000 a year), plus USD 250 a month per dependant; USD 750 a month if the applicant owns Panamanian real estate worth over USD 100,000. Couples may combine pensions per one source. A visit every two years is cited to keep the status.
routes.physical_presence: A visit every two years (secondary source)
routes.tax_note: Pensionado holders also get discounts (not researched). Panama taxes only Panama-source income.

sources.title: Pensionado Visa Panama Guide 2026

routes.name: Short Stay Remote Worker visa
routes.summary: A 9-month visa, renewable once, for remote workers earning at least USD 36,000 a year from outside Panama.
routes.requirements: Foreign-source income of at least USD 36,000 a year (USD 3,000 a month); contract with a foreign transnational company or self-employed teleworking; valid medical insurance covering Panama. Created by Executive Decree 198 of 7 May 2021. Valid 9 months, renewable once for the same period. Cancelled if the holder represents the foreign company in local activities.
routes.physical_presence: Up to 9 months per grant, renewable once
routes.tax_note: Foreign-source income is not taxable in Panama (per Mondaq).
